findings.title: Watcher goroutine panics when its backend event stream is closed
findings.body: `initWatcher` receives from `events` without checking the receive `ok` value and immediately dereferences `v`. When the backend is stopped, the SQL backend closes its event stream; receiving from that closed channel returns a nil `*WrittenEvent`, so `v.Type` panics (and subsequent loop iterations would continue receiving nil). Eager initialization now guarantees this watcher is started for every ResourceServer, including servers that never receive an RPC, so normal shutdown can crash the process. Exit the goroutine when the channel is closed and also honor `s.ctx.Done()` while sending to `out`.

findings.title: Per-key index builds can now concurrently create the same Bleve index
findings.body: Moving the cache lock to only the final map assignment permits two callers that both observed a missing index to execute `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` concurrently. For file-backed indexes they both call `bleve.New` on the same directory, which can fail due to Bleve's directory lock; for memory-backed indexes, both callers can receive distinct indexes and the last assignment silently replaces the cache entry, leaving one caller searching an index that will no longer receive watch updates. The previous broad lock at least prevented simultaneous directory creation. Use a per-resource singleflight/keyed lock and recheck the cache before creating and publishing an index.

findings.title: Search index watch goroutine also dereferences nil after stream closure
findings.body: The search initialization goroutine reads `v := <-events` forever and passes it to `handleEvent` without checking whether the event channel was closed. On backend shutdown, `WatchWriteEvents` closes the SQL stream, after which `v` is nil and `handleEvent` dereferences `evt.Type`, causing a panic. Because initialization is now performed in `NewResourceServer`, this goroutine is started unconditionally whenever search is configured, making shutdown of an otherwise unused server susceptible to this panic. Handle closed channels and tie this watch context to the server lifecycle rather than `context.Background()`.
